USER REQUEST:
Write a polynomial-time reduction from 3-Coloring to Independent Set. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is 3-Coloring and TARGET is Independent Set. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = ThreeColoring
3-Coloring (graph 3-colorability).

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...]}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.

Yes iff each vertex can be given one of 3 colours so that the two
endpoints of every edge get different colours. Not every colour has to
be used.

Edge cases: n = 0 is yes. Any graph with at most 3 vertices is yes. A
graph containing 4 mutually adjacent vertices (K4) is no.

TARGET = IndependentSet
Independent Set.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has an independent set of AT LEAST k vertices: k
vertices with no edge between any two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k > n is always no. With no edges,
every set of vertices is independent.

WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-gpd54up5
All input files are in this directory; run every command from it and write your files here. problems.py provides SOURCE and TARGET with validate(instance) only. It has NO solvers and NO instance generators.

    reduce(instance) -> instance

The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

Before submitting, check your reduction. problems.py has no solvers, so first write your own brute-force solvers for both problems from the definitions above. Then write tests in test_reduce.py that compare your solvers' answers on many small source instances and their reductions, run them, and revise until the tests pass. "command": "apply_patch <<'PATCH'
*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: reduce.py
+"""Reduction from 3-Coloring to Independent Set.
+
+The reduction is the classic one used in many textbooks:
+
+* For each vertex *v* in the original graph G we create three vertices
+  ``v_0, v_1, v_2`` in the new graph H.  These three vertices form a
+  triangle, guaranteeing that at most one of them can belong to an
+  independent set.
+* For each edge ``(u, v)`` in G and for each colour ``c`` (0,1,2) we add
+  an edge between ``u_c`` and ``v_c``.  This forbids two adjacent vertices
+  in G from taking the same colour.
+
+An independent set of size *n* in H therefore selects exactly one of the
+three copies for each original vertex, and the edges ensure that the
+selected copies correspond to a proper 3‑colouring of G.  Conversely, a
+proper 3‑colouring of G yields an independent set of size *n* by picking
+the appropriate copy for each vertex.
